newsitem.title: JAPAN: THAI RESCUE MEET TO BE FINALISED MONDAY--CHAIYAWAT.
newsitem.headline: THAI RESCUE MEET TO BE FINALISED MONDAY--CHAIYAWAT.

text.p: A meeting in Tokyo of potential donors discussing a package to ease Thailand's financial crisis will be finalised on Monday afternoon, Thai central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi told reporters.
Chaiyawat said as he emerged at the end of a morning session: "We will finalise everything this afternoon."
A World Bank official said: "Things are moving nicely," and a Canadian delegate said: "I think it was a smooth meeting."

IMF Deputy Managing Director Shigemitsu Sugisaki, asked if the IMF was satisfied Thailand's budget cuts and its fiscal consolidation measures, said: "It's up to the (IMF) board to decide if it's satisfied."
Asked if the talks would be completed on Monday, Sugisaki said: "The talks are only for one day."
Participating in the meeting are 13 countries and three multilateral financial institutions -- the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank.

Monetary sources in Washington and Tokyo have said that Japan's Export-Import Bank is likely to be the biggest single donor, followed by the IMF, other financial institutions and other nations in the Asia-Pacific region.
Thailand is looking for $12 billion to $15 billion to plug financial holes it created when it floated the baht last month after failing to defend the currency from speculative attack.
